title: Is there a reason why theater actors are able to act a whole play while not breaking character, while movie/show actors often break in laughter or misspeak their lines ?

commenti.body: A few things: Rehearsal time, stage actors get more time to know the material in and out. Improv, most TV shows enlist ways to make it funnier and the funny comes from the unexpected. The stakes, there are none in TV. The actors know they can just use another take.

Have you ever worked on a set? It’s a completely different beast than being a theatre. 

So many departments working together, often in remote locations, and you have short windows to capture ‘perfection.’ 

With the proliferation of every department having their own monitors, this whole process has gotten even slower. 

So it’s just ultimately a different animal and not really comparable in terms of the craftwork that goes into creating a performance for a live audience vs a camera

I’d add another question to this one: have you (the OP) ever preformed live? The adrenaline of a live performance is not to be underestimated. You just don’t have that juice on set. But on stage it’s enough to carry you through. 

Also when mistakes happen, the actors roll with them more because there’s no other choice.

Mostly rehearsal time. Filmed things barely get rehearsal at all compared to theater. But for theater you rehearse a lot and then you’re doing the play every night/week for weeks or months. On sets you’re jumping from scene to scene entirely out of order and sometimes not rehearsing at all.
The most impressive thing of all, in my mind, is a show like *The Oh, Hello Show* that was a live Broadway performance with a loose script but lots of improvisation, so each show was a bit different.

Yeah, just think back on doing school plays vs. shooting home movies with your friends (if you have those experiences from when you were a kid, of course). School plays went smooth for the far majority of the time as far as I remember, while even a simple half-minute take in our movies would literally take hours because people would not stop messing up and laughing. This is of course talking about amateur kids without any training, but I think the basic principle is the same for adult actors.
